packages.name: unity-hub
packages.discovery: regex on the official update feed https://public-cdn.cloud.unity3d.com/hub/prod/latest.yml: path:\s*(?<version>[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)/(?<file>UnityHubSetup-[0-9.]+-x64-msix-converter\.exe); the arm64 twin listed under files: does not match. The version is bound to the x64 converter named by the same feed entry
packages.publisherCheck: the base64 SHA-512 in latest.yml equals the locally re-hashed SHA-512 of the x64 converter; the rule is trust https + signature true, so every download must also pass Authenticode Valid. The regex provider cannot compare the feed digest itself, so that comparison was done by hand for this version

authenticode.converter: Valid, CN=Unity Technologies SF, O=Unity Technologies SF, L=San Francisco, S=California, C=US, SERIALNUMBER=3183233 (EV), thumbprint 228FB6411B0A144478C86AAA3CD9473C43A8ABA7, certificate notAfter 2027-07-18, DigiCert SHA256 RSA4096 timestamp

container.outer: PE image (32-bit stub, FileVersion 4.0.2) carrying an NSIS-3 Unicode archive, LZMA:23 solid, read by the pinned 7-Zip 26.05 as nsis
container.whatTheVendorInstallerDoes: the shell is an elevated wrapper whose PowerShell script runs Add-AppxPackage and Add-AppxProvisionedPackage on UnityHub.msix, then verifies the registered package identity and removes an older Win32 Hub. None of it is executed or installed by the package: only the MSIX container is expanded as a plain ZIP

msix.identity: UnityTechnologies.UnityHub 4.0.2.65535 x64, Publisher CN=Unity Technologies SF (EV subject), Application Id UnityHub, Executable app\Unity Hub.exe, EntryPoint Windows.FullTrustApplication
msix.declarationsNotReproducedWhenUnpacked: unityhub:// protocol, unityhub.exe app execution alias, startup task, uap13 AutoUpdate App Installer pointer, Desktop shortcut repair
msix.zipMethods: 437 Deflate and 40 Store entries, all decodable by the client's yauzl path
msix.signature: AppxSignature.p7x and AppxMetadata/CodeIntegrity.cat ship inside the container; neither is validated by the package, the outer Authenticode check is the enforced publisher gate

packages.nested: $9/UnityHub.msix expanded as zip without a stripPrefix: the container root also holds AppxManifest.xml, AppxBlockMap.xml, [Content_Types].xml, AppxMetadata/, AppxSignature.p7x, Assets/ (18 PNG) and 5 .pri files, so a stripPrefix would be rejected as entries outside the prefix. These 28 package-metadata files (about 7 MB) are inert and ship as-is

layout.knownExpandedBytesNote: includes the 62,045,541-byte intermediate MSIX layer charged by checkLayout
layout.checksumsJson: app/checksums.json lists SHA-512 for the 440 app/assets files; the executables are not listed

entryNames.issue: MSIX zip entry names are URI-encoded, so 7-Zip names the main program app\Unity%20Hub.exe (AppxBlockMap.xml and the manifest use app\Unity Hub.exe). Nested steps support only stripPrefix, so the package keeps the encoded name; app/UnityLicensingClient_V1/Third%20Party%20Notices.md is the only other affected entry
entryNames.triage: the Hub binary contains 'Unity Hub.exe' only as the VERSIONINFO OriginalFilename; it locates itself through current_exe(), and unity.exe finds the Hub through registry keys and common install paths or its own directory. No hard-coded own-file-name dependency was found by ASCII/UTF-16 scan
entryNames.consequence: bin and the shortcut target app/Unity%20Hub.exe; renaming would need a files map on a nested step, which neither the source validator nor client 0.4.37 accept today

commandModel.unity: the Unity CLI bundled by Hub 4 (own FileVersion 1.0.1); it locates an installed Hub and can itself download the Hub installer from the same CDN, which was not exercised
commandModel.desktop: Unity Hub shortcut declared; requires separate integrate --desktop preview/confirmation

stateModel.userData: native %APPDATA%\UnityHub and %LOCALAPPDATA%\UnityHub (hub.db, accounts.db, JSON blobs, logs); the MSIX declares these folders unvirtualized so every Hub flavour shares them, and the unpackaged tree uses them directly

isolatedInstall.pikoHome: temporary directory with a loopback HTTP copy of this source (index.json and package documents only)
isolatedInstall.installed: iso/unity-hub@4.0.2; the client fetched its own pinned full 7-Zip 26.05 helper for the NSIS layer
isolatedInstall.installedTreeVsOfficialMsix: 477/477 files byte-identical to the 7-Zip expansion of UnityHub.msix; the only extra file is the .piko-install.json receipt (kind portable, verified true)

packages.updateModel: a new Hub version is discovered from latest.yml, downloaded, signature-checked and expanded through the same nested step; a release that renames the converter, moves UnityHub.msix or drops app/Unity%20Hub.exe, unity.exe or the licensing client is blocked and the published version is kept

rejectedAlternatives: Unity Hub 3.22.6 (UnityHubSetup-3.22.6-x64.exe, 193,133,232 bytes): a classic NSIS Electron installer that would extract without renaming, but it is the last 3.x release and its built-in updater moves users to the 4.x MSIX converter

An admin recipe that runs the signed converter: faithful MSIX registration, but it needs an elevated terminal, registers a package that piko cannot deregister on uninstall and provisions every other account

Unity Editor installers without the Hub: the archive API services.api.unity.com/unity/editor/release/v1/releases gives version-bound UnitySetup64-<version>.exe links with MD5 integrity, but the editors are 2.62 GiB (2020.3.49f1) to 4.2 GiB (6000.3.29f1), above the 2 GiB download ceiling enforced by this source and by the client; only 2019.4.41f2 (1.76 GiB) and older would fit
